column2: Peel and dice the potato and boil in boiling water for 12–15 minutes.
Steam the whiting in the basket for 8 minutes.
Mash the potato, whiting and butter with a fork.
Finely grate the carrot.
Melt the butter in a small pan and cook the carrot for 3 minutes.
Add the couscous and stir.
Add the hot water and turn off the heat; leave covered for 10 minutes.
Fluff with a fork to break up any lumps.
Mash the banana smooth with a fork.
Add the egg and oats and whisk; leave for 5 minutes.
Heat a non-stick pan over low heat; drop in small pancakes with a spoon.
When the underside is golden, turn and cook the other side for 1–2 minutes.
Cut one in half: there should be no runny egg inside.
Dice the meat small; trim off fat and sinew.
Put the meat and water in a pan and bring to the boil; skim off the foam.
Cook covered over low heat for 30 minutes.
Dice the vegetables small and add them; cook for 20 more minutes.
Shred the meat finely; mash it lightly with the vegetables.
Split the white part of the leek lengthways and wash between the layers well; chop very finely.
Soften the leek in olive oil in a small pan for 3 minutes.
Add the rice and water; cook over low heat for 20 minutes until very soft.
Wash the strawberries in plenty of water and remove the stalks.
Mash well with a fork.
Strawberries can cause redness around the mouth in some babies; if giving for the first time, watch for 3 days.
Rub the quinoa under plenty of water in a fine sieve; this removes the bitter taste.
Bring the quinoa, carrot and water to the boil; cook over low heat for 18 minutes.
Peel the tomato and remove the seeds; chop it small with the courgette.
Put the vegetables, bulgur and water in a pan and bring to the boil.
Cook over low heat, stirring now and then, for 15 minutes until soft.
Steam the salmon in the basket for 10 minutes.
Mash the potato, salmon and butter with a fork.
Wash the spinach in plenty of water; boil for 3 minutes, drain and chop finely.
Mash the hard-boiled egg yolk with a fork.
Mix with the spinach and butter.
If too thick, add 1–2 spoonfuls of cooking water.
Wash the rice; finely grate the courgette.
Put the rice, courgette and water in a pan and bring to the boil.
Cook over low heat, stirring now and then, for 20 minutes until the rice is very soft.
Finely grate the carrot; shred the chicken very finely.
Bring the unsalted cooking stock to the boil and cook the carrot for 5 minutes.
Add the vermicelli and cook for 7 minutes until very soft.
Add the chicken and heat for 1 minute.
If needed, mash lightly with a fork.
Peel the courgette and dice it small.
Steam in the basket for 8 minutes.
When lukewarm, add the unsalted curd cheese and mix.
Peel the apple and remove the core; cut thick slices.
Arrange the slices spaced out on the tray and sprinkle with cinnamon.
If it doesn't crush when pressed with a finger, bake 5 more minutes; hard apple is a choking risk.
Mix the oats, carrot and egg yolk and leave for 5 minutes.
Make small flat patties and arrange on the tray.
Bake for 15 minutes; the centre should be dry and firm.
Wash the lentils; peel and finely grate the carrot.
Put the lentils, carrot and water in a pan and bring to the boil; skim off the foam.
Add the bulgur and cook for 5 more minutes.
Remove from the heat and leave covered for 10 minutes.
Mash lightly with a fork; from 9 months small grains can remain.
Cook covered over low heat for 40 minutes.
Dice the potato and courgette small and add them; cook for 15 more minutes.
Shred the meat finely and mash it with the vegetables.
Mix the rice flour with cold water until lump-free; put it in a pan with the courgette.
Cook for 10 minutes, stirring constantly.
Remove from the heat and cool for 5 minutes.
Add the yoghurt and stir; don't boil it or it will curdle.
Mash the potato and broccoli well with a fork.
Add the oats and knead; if too soft, add 1 more spoonful of oats.
Check the date for its stone and remove it; chop finely.
Put the oats, date and water in a small pan.
Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, for 6 minutes.
Adjust the consistency with boiled water or breast milk.
The date sweetens it; don't add any sugar.
Wash the spinach and chop very finely.
Whisk the egg and add the spinach.
Cook covered for 3–4 minutes; turn over and cook for 1–2 more minutes.
Let it cool and cut into strips.
Shred the boiled chicken very finely.
Mash the avocado with a fork.
Mix the chicken and avocado.
If too thick, soften with the chicken cooking water.
Peel the carrot and cut sticks the length and thickness of a little finger.
Cook the sticks for 15–18 minutes.
Press with your fingers: if it crushes easily it's ready; hard carrot is a choking risk.
Cut the broccoli with its stalk to a length the baby can hold; wash.
Cook for 8–10 minutes.
The floret should be soft enough to crush with a finger.
Let the baby hold it by the stalk and eat.
Choose an avocado that is ripe but not falling apart.
Peel the avocado and cut long, finger-thick slices that fit in the baby's palm.
Spread ground oats on a plate and roll the slices in them; they won't be slippery and are easier to grip.
Put 2–3 slices in front of the baby.
Wash and peel the pear and remove the core.
Cut thick slices that fit in the baby's palm.
Cook the slices for 5–6 minutes until they crush easily between your fingers.
Rinse the pan and the storage container with boiling water; a clean container helps the yoghurt set.
Bring the milk to the boil, stirring constantly, and remove from the heat.
Cool to 45°C: you should be able to keep your little finger in it for 10 seconds.
Mix the starter smooth with a ladle of warm milk, add to the pan and stir.
Cover the container and wrap it in a blanket; leave in a warm, undisturbed place for 6–8 hours.
Once set, put it in the fridge; use within 4–5 days.
Full-fat plain yoghurt can be given from 6 months; cow's milk as a drink only after 1 year.
Wash and peel the peach and remove the stone.
If firm, steam for 3 minutes to soften.
Peel and finely grate the apple.
Mix the oats, yoghurt and apple in a container with a lid.
Leave covered in the fridge overnight; the oats soften.
In the morning bring it to room temperature for 15 minutes.
If it has thickened, add 1–2 spoonfuls of breast milk.
Serve with a spoon; use within 24 hours.
Wash the rice; put it in a pan with the water and cook over low heat for 20 minutes until very soft.
Whisk the yoghurt and egg yolk smooth in a separate bowl.
Temper it by adding a few spoonfuls of the hot soup to the yoghurt, a little at a time.
Pour the mixture into the pan, stirring constantly.
Bring just to the boil, stirring constantly; the egg yolk must be fully cooked.
Add the butter and remove from the heat.
Shred and finely chop the boiled chicken.
Mash the boiled courgette with a fork.
Combine the chicken, courgette and yoghurt.
Peel the pear, steam for 5 minutes and let cool.
Mash the pear with a fork.
Add the unsalted curd cheese and mix.
If too thick, add a little breast milk or formula.
The curd cheese must be made from pasteurised milk and unsalted.
Wash the fruit in plenty of water.
Mash the banana; chop the strawberries very small or mash them.
Strawberries can cause redness around the mouth in some babies; if giving for the first time, watch closely.
